<section class="teaching-page">
  <h1 class="teaching-page-title">Teaching</h1>

  <div class="teaching-statement">
    <p>
      I teach applied statistics and quantitative methods for decision-making at the undergraduate level. My approach emphasizes building intuition before formalism: students work with real datasets from the outset, learn to formulate testable hypotheses, and develop the ability to interpret statistical evidence critically. I use a combination of lecture slides, hands-on R workshops, and applied exercises drawn from business and policy contexts.
    </p>
  </div>

  <!-- ═══ Course 1 ═══ -->
  <div class="course-card">
    <div class="course-header">
      <div class="course-icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-chart-column"></i></div>
      <div>
        <h2>Estadística para la Toma de Decisiones</h2>
        <p class="course-meta">
          <span><i class="fa-solid fa-building-columns"></i> Universidad Icesi, Cali</span>
          <span><i class="fa-solid fa-users"></i> Business Analytics Program (Undergraduate)</span>
          <span><i class="fa-solid fa-calendar"></i> 2025–present</span>
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="course-body">
      <p>
        This course introduces probability, statistical inference, and hypothesis testing as tools for evidence-based decision-making in business and policy contexts. Students learn to move from descriptive summaries to causal questions, working with real-world datasets in R.
      </p>
      <div class="course-topics">
        <span class="course-topic">Probability &amp; distributions</span>
        <span class="course-topic">Estimation &amp; confidence intervals</span>
        <span class="course-topic">Hypothesis testing</span>
        <span class="course-topic">Simple &amp; multiple regression</span>
        <span class="course-topic">Applied R workshops</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- ═══ Course 2: Impact Evaluation training ═══ -->
  <div class="course-card">
    <div class="course-header">
      <div class="course-icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-microscope"></i></div>
      <div>
        <h2>Introduction to Counterfactual Impact Evaluation</h2>
        <p class="course-meta">
          <span><i class="fa-solid fa-building-columns"></i> Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT</span>
          <span><i class="fa-solid fa-users"></i> Professional training for researchers</span>
          <span><i class="fa-solid fa-calendar"></i> 2023</span>
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="course-body">
      <p>
        A training module designed for CGIAR researchers on when to use impact evaluation, which methods fit different contexts, and what data requirements each approach demands. Covers the logic of counterfactuals, randomized controlled trials, difference-in-differences, and propensity score matching.
      </p>
      <a href="https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/c917623f-0bf1-4f10-b23d-51392de83e78" target="_blank" class="tl-link">Training materials (CGSpace) →</a>

  </div>
